name: Helix Biosystems Meningeal Pressure Dressing
description:
The Meningeal Pressure Dressing is a rigid semi-circular cranial appliance that fits over the top and sides of the skull, secured by four self-tightening anchor straps that locate against the zygomatic arches and occipital ridge. Its inner surface is lined with a lattice of piezoelectric pressure sensors and a distributed array of micro-needles — each no longer than two millimeters — that penetrate the scalp to deliver a proprietary osmotic compound called Durasolv directly into the subgaleal space. Durasolv works by drawing interstitial fluid away from the meninges through osmotic gradient manipulation, reducing intracranial pressure without the need for surgical decompression. The device monitors pressure in real time and modulates Durasolv delivery in response, attempting to hold intracranial pressure within a survivable range for up to six hours.

The Crown's distinctive quality is its accessibility: it requires no surgical training to apply, no sterile field, and no diagnostic imaging beyond what the device itself provides through its pressure-sensor array. A medic can fit it in under ninety seconds. Helix Biosystems designed it explicitly for scenarios where traumatic brain injury occurs far from neurosurgical infrastructure — which in Meridian 88 describes most of the city. The device cannot resolve the underlying injury, but it can extend the window in which resolution is possible, and in a city where the nearest licensed neurosurgeon may be four transit hours away, that window is the difference between outcome and obituary.

The Meningeal Pressure Dressing is standard issue in Arcturus Defense Solutions forward medical kits — a procurement relationship that has made Helix Biosystems quietly wealthy — and is distributed through licensed channels to paramedic services in the inner and mid-ring districts. Outer-ring circulation is patchier, and in the furthest corridors of Meridian 88's periphery, the device is more likely to be found secondhand, recalibrated by someone who understood enough of the underlying engineering to make it functional again. These recalibrated units carry the street name 'The Halo Press,' and their reliability is a subject of significant debate.

cultural_context: In Meridian 88, traumatic brain injury is among the most common causes of preventable death — the city's density, its violence, and its architecture conspire to produce head trauma at rates that overwhelm neurosurgical capacity. The Meningeal Pressure Dressing has become, in the inner and mid-ring districts, a symbol of the kind of care that is available: not curative, not elegant, but present. Wearing one on the way to a hospital is a recognizable sight, and the semi-circular shape has entered visual slang — to 'be in the crown' means to be in a situation that might still be recoverable, but is running out of time. In the outer ring, the recalibrated Halo Press units are worn with a different kind of significance: proof that someone out here cared enough to keep the hardware working.
known_users: Recalibration technicians supplying the Halo Press market
story_hooks: A batch of Meningeal Pressure Dressings distributed to outer-ring paramedic stations has a Durasolv formulation that behaves differently from the standard compound — patients stabilize faster and more completely than the device should be capable of, but two have reported persistent auditory phenomena they cannot account for after the device was removed.

A Halo Press unit recovered from a dead ganger contains sensor logs that place it at three separate incident sites over the past month — each site the location of a disappearance that was never investigated.

Helix Biosystems is quietly recalling a specific production run of the device without public announcement. A paramedic who received the recall notice wants to know why, and whether the units already deployed should be pulled from service.

A neurosurgeon working in the outer ring has been modifying Halo Press units to extend their operational duration beyond six hours using a secondary Durasolv reservoir. Her patients survive longer than they should. She needs someone to source the parts without asking questions.
